0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part I ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 14 September 1978, after the draft finalized by the_Rcsistors Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Tclecommunication Division Council. 0.2 This standard ( Part I ) lays down test methods requirements for judging the performance of fixed power used in electronic and telecommunication equipment. and general resistors to be

0.2.1 DLmmsional and specific requirements of various types of fixed power resistors are covered in the subsequent parts of this standard. 0.3 In the preparation the following: of this standard, assistance has been derived from

Dot: 40 ( Central Office ) 331 -Draft, fixed power selection of methods of tests and general requirements. national Electrotechnical Commission. JSS:

resistors, Inter-

50402 ( 1972 ) -Detail specification for resistor, fixed, high surface temperature. Directorate of Standardization, Department of Dcfence Production, Ministry of Defence, New Delhi.

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed orcalculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part I ) prescribes the requirements and methods of test for judging the electrical, mechanical, and climatic properties of fixed power resistors with rated dissipation from 2.5 W up to and including 250 W, and which are provided with a cover or coating for environmental protection.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( wised ).

IS t 8909 ( Part I ) - 1978 1.1.1 Subsequent parts of this standard cover the performance requirements and dimensions of the fixed resistors of .rating from 2.5 W up to and including 250 W.

4.1 Rated Resistance

-

The nreferred values of rated resistance shall be specifi:d in IS : 824-1965*, depending on the

4.2 Tolerance on Rated Resistance - The preferred values of tolerance on rated resistance shall be 5 and 10 percent. 4.3 Rated Dissipation -The preferred values of rated dissipation shall be chosen from the R5 and RIO series of IS : 1076-1967t. Unless otherwise specified, the dissipation shall be given with reference to an ambient temperature of 70�C. 4.4 Limiting Element Voltage -- The value of limiting element shall be chosen from the following: 100, 150, 200,250, 350, 500, 750, 1 000, 1 250, 2 500, 2 750, 3 000, and 3 500 volts 5. MATERIAL, CONSTRUCTION 1 500, voltage

1 750, 2 000,

AND WORKMANSHIP

5.1 Material - Resistors shall be constructed from the most suitable materials which shall be free from flaws. All materials used in the construction of the resjstors shall be such as not susceptible to any mutual chemical reaction over the entire range of climatic conditions in which the resirtor is designed to operate. 5.1.1 Materials used in the moulding and coating of reristors shall not support combustion. 5,2 Construction 5.2.1 The body of the resistor shall be free from cracks, holes, chips 01 malformations. The wire leads shall be unbroken, not crushed or nicked. 5.2.2 Electrical connections shall be mechanically continuous both before and after soldering. secure and electrically

5.3 Soldering - Generally, non-corrosive fluxes shall bc used for soldering the leads of resistors and it shall be ensured that all excess fluxes have been satisfactorily removed. 5.4 Workmanship - All resistors shall be manufactured in a thoroughly workman like manner and in accordance with the current engineering practice.
*Preferred tl'referred values ior resistors and capacitora. numbers (JSrrr r&ion ).

6.1 The style reference used shall be abbreviations to identify a particular type,of resistor and shall be composed as given in the following example: Example: FRPl-2.5 FR denotes fixed resistor of P denotes general purpose, power 1 denotes a particular type of resistor ~(see subsequent part this standard ) 2.5 denotes rated dissipation in watts. 7. MARKING 7.1 The fdllowing marking information is required in order of importance given below: a) Rated resistance; b) Tolerance on rated resistance; c) Rated dissipation; d) Week ( or month ) and year of manufacture; e) Style reference; and f) Manufacturer's type designation, if any. 7.1.1 When a coded marking is used, it shall be in accordance IS : 8186-1976;. with

7.2 The resistars shall be clearly marked with items (a), (b) and (c) given in 7.1 and with as many other items as is practical. 7.3 The package containing the resistor(s) all the information listed in 7.1. shall be clearly marked with that no

7.4 Any additional marking shall be applied in such a manner confusion may arise. 7.5 The resistors may also be marked with the Standard Mark.

NOTE - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made there. under. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that Details of conditions under which a licence for standard as a further safeguard. the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturets or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

8.2.5 Drying - When drying is called for in this standard the resistors shall be conditioned before measurements are made using Procedure I or Procedure II as specified. Procedure Procedure I : For 24f4 hours in an oven at a temperature of 55&2?C and at a relative humidity not exceeding 20 percent. II : For 96 f4 hours in an oven at 100 f5'C.

82-5.1 The resistors shall be allowed to cool in a desiccator using a suitable desiccant such as activated alumina or silica gel and shall be kept therein from the time of removal from the oven to the beginning of the specified tests. 8.3 Electrical Tests

8.3.2.1 This test shall be performed using one of the following three The V-block methods, as prescribed in the relevant detail specification. method shall be that preferred for resistors without mounting devices.

4

V-block m&hod - The resistor shall be clamped in the trough of a 909 metallic V-block of such size that the resistor body does not extend beyond the extremities of the block. The clamping force shall be such as to guarantee adequate contact between the resistor and the block. The clamping force is to be chosen in such a wav or damage to , that no destruction the resistor occurs. that the distance The terminations shall be so positioned is not between the terminations and any point of the V-block less than: The radius of the resistor body 11 For cylindrical resistors minus the radius of the circumscribed circle of the terminations ( the larger circle when the two terminations have different dimensions ) 10

Half the smaller side of the reuistor body minus the radius of the circumscribed circle of the terminations (the larger circle when the two terminations have different dimensions ) at its emer-

Any out of centre positioning of the termination gence from the resistor body shall he ignored.

II) Foil method ( alternative method fbr resistors without mounting devices ) - A metal foil shall be wrapped closely around the body of the resistor. For resistors not having axial terminations, a space of 1 to 1.5 mm shall be left between the edge of the foil and each termination. For resistors having axial terminations, the foil shall be wrapped around the whole body of the resistor protruding by at least 5 mm from each end, provided that the minimum space of 1 mm between the foil and the termination can be maintained. The ends of foil shall not be folded over the ends of the resistor. c) Method for resistors with mounting d&es-The resistor shall be mounted in its normal manner on a metal plate (or between metal plates ) which extends at least 12.5 mm beyond the mounting face of the resistor in all directions. 8.3.2.2 The insulation resistance shall be measured between both termination of the resistor connected together as one pole and the V-block or metal foil or mounting plate(s), as the other pole. The measuring voltage shall be either 100 & 15 V dc for resistors with a limiting element voltage less than 500 V or 500 f 5 V dcfor resistors with a limiting element voltage equal to or more than 500 V. The error of measurement shall not exceed f10 percent.

The voltage shall be applied for 1 minute or for such shorter time as is necessary to obtain a stable reading; the insulation resistance shall be read at the end of that period. 8.3.2.3 When measured as specified in 8.3.2.2 using one of the methods of mounting described in 8.3.2.1 the insulation resistance shall be not less than that prescribed in the relevant detail specification. 8.3.3 Voltage Proof ( Applicablesfor Insulaled Typts Onb )

8.3.4.5 The temperature characteristic of resistance, determined as described above, shall not exceed that specified in relevant detail specification for the appropriate category temperature. 8.3.5
Temperaturn Rise

8.3.5.1 Resistors having a rated resistance equal to or less than the critical resistance value shall be subjected to this test.

8.3.5.2 The resistor shall be mounted horizontally. For wirewound resistors, the axis of the resistance winding shall be horizontal. Connections shall be made in the usual manner as for endurance test. For resistors with soldering tags, copper wire of approximately 1.0 mm diameter shall be used for connecting the resistors. The detail specification shall prescribe any special mounting arrangements. 8.3.5.3 The ambient temperature for the test shall be between 15�C and 35�C. There shall be no air circulation other than that produced by the convection current caused by the heated resistor. 8.3.5.4 The rated voltage shall be applied. 8.3.5.5 The temperature at the hottest point of the resistor shall be -measured after temperature equilibrium has been attained. The temperature measuring device shall be of such dimensions as not to affect the measurement. 8.3.5.6 The temperature rise shall not exceed the value prescribed the relevant detail specification. in

The value of the voltage and the duration of its application shall be as prescribed in the relevant detail specification. Connections shall be made in test. The change of resistance compared with the value measured in 8.4.5.2 shall not exceed the value specified in the relevant detail specification. 8.4.6 Solderabilip - The resistors shall be subjected to one of the procedures specified in 7.18 of IS : 589- k9ol*. The relevant detail specification shall prescribe which method is preferred and shall give the additional information as required. Where the detail specification states that terminations are suitable for use with printed wiring, they shall be tested at a point, not more than 3.5 to 4 mm from where the termination emerges from the body of the resistor. In the case of the solder globule method ( under consideration ), the relevant detail specification shall indicate what the soldering time shall be: 8.4.7 Vibration - The resistors shall be subjected to the vibration ( fatigue ) test in accordance with 7.6 of IS : 589-1961*, with the severities as' specified in the relevant detail specification. 8.4.7.1 Resistors shall be mounted by their normal means. Where this is by axial wire terminations the distance between the resistor body and the mounting point on the termination shall be 6f 1 mm. 8.4.7.2 When specified in the relevant detail specification an electrical measurement shall be made to determine intermittent contact or open or short circuit. The duration of the measurement shall be the time needed for one sweep of the frequency range from one frequency extreme to the other. 8.4.7.3 After the test, the resistors shall be visually examined. There shall be no visible damage. The resistance shall then be measured. The change in resistance value shall not exceed the limits specified in the relevant detail specification. 8.4.8 BumpThe resistor shall be accordance with 7.5.1 of IS : 589-1961*, the relevent detail specification.

8.6.3.1 The resistors having rated dissipation up to 16 W shall be subjected to this test at temperature of rating and upper category temperature and for resistors with rated dissipation above 16 W, the test shall be conducted under atmospheric conditions for testing.

A voltage shall be applied to the resistors in cycles of 14 hours ON and 4 hour OFF throughout the test. The use of ac or dc shall comply with the requirements of the endurance tests at rating temperature. IS : 8909 ( Part I ) - 1978 Those resistors which are dissipating power during this test shall be mounted in the test chamber at 200�C in the manner required in the endurance test at rated temperature. All other resistors shall be placed in the test chamber at their appropriate temperatures in such a manner that the spacing between resistors is at least one diameter. When the resistors are dissipating power, they shall be mounted in the same manner as specified in 8.6.3.2(a). There shall be no undue draught over the resistors. If forced air circulation is used in the test chamber, the resistors shall be protected so that there is no draught, other than by natural convection, over the resistors. The size of the testing chamber and the number of resistors under test shall be such that when all resistors are fully loaded the heat produced by them shall be less than that required to maintain the atmosphere in the chamber at the upper category temperature so that the temperature can still be controlled by the heating elements. The temperature controlling elements shall be suitably spaced from the resistors and shall be shielded so as not to be directly influenced by the radiation of the resistors. It shall be assumed in this test that the ambient temperature of the resistors is the same as the upper category temperature. After approximately 48, 168, 250, 500 and 1 000 hours, the resistors shall be removed from the chamber and allowed to recover under standard atmospheric conditions for testing for not less than 1 hour and not more than 2 hours. The removal from the chamber shall take place at the end of the half-hour OFF period, for those resistors which are dissipating power. The resistors shall then be visually examined. visible damage. The resistance shall then be measured. The change of resistance with respect to the value initially measured in each of the succeeding measurement shall not exceed the value prescribed in the relevant detail specification for the corresponding endurance test at 70�C or at room temperature.
